_comment: Hand-curated homeopathy layer: evidence framing, toxic-source flags, and symptom→rubric hints (hints are suggestions for clinician selection; rubric paths verified to exist in Repertorium Publicum).

evidence.summary: A systematic assessment by Australia's NHMRC concluded there are no health conditions for which there is reliable evidence that homeopathy is effective.

source.reference: NHMRC Information Paper: Evidence on the effectiveness of homeopathy for treating health conditions (2015)

evidence.summary: The Royal Australian College of General Practitioners' position (2025) describes the certainty of evidence for homeopathy as low or very low.

source.reference: RACGP position on homeopathy (informed by the Natural Therapies Review 2024)

evidence.summary: Homeopathy organisations have published methodological critiques of the NHMRC review; these critiques are recorded here so the disagreement is visible rather than resolved by this tool.

source.reference: Conflict disclosure — critiques published in homeopathy literature (e.g., the journal Homeopathy)

evidence.summary: Repertory grades (1–3) reflect the typographic emphasis given by repertory authors to remedy–symptom associations recorded in provings and clinical reports. They are not probabilities and not measures of efficacy.

regulatory.text: Homoeopathy is a recognised system of medicine in India, regulated by the National Commission for Homoeopathy under the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020. Recognition as a system of practice is a regulatory fact and is not evidence of clinical efficacy.

source.reference: National Commission for Homoeopathy — Acts, rules and regulations

caseTakingQuestions.question: What makes the complaint better or worse (time of day, weather, motion, rest, pressure, warmth/cold, eating)?
How exactly does the complaint feel (throbbing, pressing, burning, stitching, bursting)?
Which side is affected, and does it move from side to side?
Was there a clear causation or trigger (exposure to sun, cold, grief, fright, overeating)?
What other symptoms occur at the same time (nausea, thirst, chill, perspiration)?
Any characteristic mental/emotional state accompanying the complaint?
Is there a characteristic time of onset or aggravation?
